item.test_conditions: Room temperature compressive testing, ASTM G65 wear tests, electrochemical tests in 0.5 M H2SO4
item.structure_change: BCC solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases (Cr2Nb, (Fe,Cr)Nb) and oxides (NbVO4-VO); grain coarsening and Laves phase dissolution at higher temperatures
item.property_change: Compressive strength 2700–2870 MPa; hardness decreased with temperature increase; wear resistance of carburized layer superior to bulk
item.attributed_mechanism: Laves phases and oxides precipitate due to Fe impurities and oxygen affinity; higher temperature promotes reverse dissolution of Laves phases and higher diffusion
quotes: The MA powders' phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution.
The solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases under the sintering, such as Cr 2 Nb and (Fe, Cr)Nb, and NbVO 4 -VO oxides mixture.
The temperature increase to 1400 °C led to a grain coarsening of the BCC phase and decreased the Laves phase content accompanied by precipitation at the grain boundaries.

records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: Mechanically alloyed (MA) CrMoNbWV equiatomic powder. Intervention: Spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1200 °C, 1300 °C, and 1400 °C. Processing: SPS in graphite die (Ø40 mm) at 50 MPa pressure, 5 min isothermal hold at max temperature. Test conditions: Room temperature compressive testing, ASTM G65 wear tests, electrochemical tests in 0.5 M H2SO4. Structure change: BCC solid solution partially decomposed to Laves phases (Cr2Nb, (Fe,Cr)Nb) and oxides (NbVO4-VO); grain coarsening and Laves phase dissolution at higher temperatures. Property change: Compressive strength 2700–2870 MPa; hardness decreased with temperature increase; wear resistance of carburized layer superior to bulk. Mechanism: Laves phases and oxides precipitate due to Fe impurities and oxygen affinity; higher temperature promotes reverse dissolution of Laves phases and higher diffusion. Evidence: measured. Quote: "The MA powders' phase composition was found to be represented by body-centered-cubic (BCC) solid solution."

item.processing: SPS at 50 MPa, 5 min hold, varying max temperature from 1200 to 1400 °C
item.test_conditions: Microstructural analysis via SEM and XRD
item.structure_change: Laves phase volume fraction decreased from 41.6% to 11.5%; oxides coagulated and localized along grain boundaries; grain size increased to up to 15 µm
item.property_change: Hardness decreased due to grain growth; compressive strength remained relatively stable (2700–2870 MPa)
item.attributed_mechanism: Increase of sintering temperature leads to reverse dissolution of Laves phases and higher diffusion of elements
quotes: The increase of the sintering temperature led to a gradual decrease in the calculated volume fraction of the Laves phases, which was 21.5 and 11.5% at 1300 °C and 1400 °C, respectively.
The temperature increase up to 1400 °C led to the samples' recrystallization, resulting in equiaxial grains of a solid solution with a size of up to 15 µm.
Figure 2 shows a growth of the BCC-matrix grains accompanies the increase in the sintering temperature, leading to a decrease of the hardness.

item.test_conditions: Electrochemical corrosion tests in 0.5 M H2SO4 at room temperature
item.structure_change: Laves phase content decreased significantly; oxide morphology changed from splintery to circular; carburized layer thickness increased (18–75 µm)
item.property_change: Corrosion current density (i_corr) decreased from 2.81 µA/cm² (1200 °C) to 0.88 µA/cm² (1400 °C); open circuit potential (E_OCP) shifted positively
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher temperature promotes diffusion and reduces Laves phase content, improving passivation ability
quotes: The increase of the SPS temperature provided a positive shift of the E OCP and a decrease of i corr , leading to the good corrosion resistance of the SPS samples obtained at 1300–1400 °C, in H 2 SO 4 solution.
The SPS temperature increase resulted in a decrease of i corr , where the values were 0.91, 0.66, and 0.21 µA/cm 2 .
On the contrary, the E OCP shifted to higher positive values from 100 to 276 mV, respectively.

item.processing: SPS at 1200–1400 °C leading to interaction with graphite die carbon
item.test_conditions: Wear tests (ASTM G65) and electrochemical tests on carburized layer vs bulk
item.structure_change: Carburization of surface layer (18–75 µm thick) with intercalated carbon atoms and formation of HEA carbides
item.property_change: Bulk loss of carburized layer 0.001 cm³ (vs 0.0035–0.0048 cm³ for bulk); wear resistance 300% higher than bulk HEA
item.attributed_mechanism: BCC-lattice strain caused by intercalation of carbon atoms and fine-dispersed HEA carbides
quotes: Under SPS, the HEA powder interacted with the carbon of the equipment that led to carburization of the surface layer.
The bulk loss of the sintered samples' carburized layer was 0.001 cm 3 , which exceeded the values for nickel bonded tungsten carbide (0.003 cm 3 ).
The difference between the values for the carburized layer and the bulk HEA is 300%, indicating the superior wear resistance of the carburized layer compared to the conventional hard alloys.

item.test_conditions: Compressive strength testing at room temperature
item.structure_change: Laves phase volume fraction decreased from 41.6% to 11.5%; oxide particle size increased significantly
item.property_change: Compressive strength remained in range 2700–2870 MPa; plasticity remained low due to coarse oxide inclusions acting as crack initiation sources
item.attributed_mechanism: Coarse oxide inclusions act as crack initiation sources and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix
quotes: The sintered samples exhibit the compressive strength of 2700–2870 MPa.
The increase of the sintering temperature does not significantly influence the sample strength.

However, the oxide particle size significantly increases, as shown in Figure 2 . The coarse inclusions can act as a crack initiation source and cause fractures in the BCC-matrix that leads to a decrease of the HEA plasticity.

item.processing: SPS at 1400 °C (CrMoNbWV) vs prior arc melting (WNbMoTaV)
item.structure_change: CrMoNbWV has BCC structure with low Laves phase content (11.5%); WNbMoTaV has different lattice parameter
item.property_change: CrMoNbWV density 10.55 g/cm³ vs WNbMoTaV 12.42 g/cm³; comparable mechanical and corrosive properties
item.attributed_mechanism: Reduced density due to element selection (Cr, V vs Ta, W)
quotes: The CrMoNbWV HEA has comparable mechanical and corrosive properties with the WNbMoTaV type HEA, but at the same time has a reduced density: CrMoNbWV—10.55 g/cm 3 , WNbMoTaV—12.42 g/cm 3 .
Calculation of the crystal density of equiatomic alloys by mass and lattice parameter showed that the CrMoNbWV HEA density with the lattice parameter a = 3.106 Å was 10.55 g/cm 3 .
For the WNbMoTaV alloy, the crystal density at the lattice parameter a = 3.186 Å [ [19] ] was 12.42 g/cm 3 .

item.test_conditions: Electrochemical tests on carburized layer in 0.5 M H2SO4
item.structure_change: Carburized layer thickness increased; fine-dispersed carbides formed; passivation region ΔE narrowed or absent
item.property_change: Corrosion current density decreased from 0.91 µA/cm² (1200 °C) to 0.21 µA/cm² (1400 °C); chemical stability increased
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher temperature leads to higher C diffusion and formation of fine-dispersed carbides, though passivation region is reduced
quotes: The SPS temperature increase resulted in a decrease of i corr , where the values were 0.91, 0.66, and 0.21 µA/cm 2 .
The carburized layer of the HEA SPS-samples obtained at 1400 °C exhibited an almost linear increase of the current density under the increase of the potential.
The results showed that the chemical stability of the carburized layer increases with increasing sintering temperature.

item.structure_change: Grain size increased; Laves phase volume decreased; oxide particle size increased
item.property_change: Compressive strength remained stable (2700–2870 MPa); plasticity remained low
item.attributed_mechanism: High volume fraction of brittle Laves phases and oxides localized at grain boundaries promotes crack initiation
quotes: The samples' low plasticity was caused by the high volume fraction of Cr 2 Nb, (Fe, Cr)Nb Laves phases, and NbVO 4 –VO oxides, which localized at the grain boundaries.
These phases were brittle at room temperature, and their localization promoted a crack initiation and propagation along the grain boundaries resulting in a decrease of the HEA plasticity.
The increase of the sintering temperature does not significantly influence the sample strength.

item.structure_change: Carburized layer thickness increased; fine-dispersed carbides formed; passivation region ΔE disappeared at 1400 °C
item.property_change: i_corr decreased from 0.91 to 0.21 µA/cm²; E_OCP shifted from 100 to 276 mV
item.attributed_mechanism: Higher C diffusion and fine-dispersed carbides formation; gradual dissolution of alloy components
quotes: The carburized layer of the HEA SPS-samples obtained at 1400 °C exhibited an almost linear increase of the current density under the increase of the potential.
A clearly defined passivation plateau was almost absent, and the alloy components gradually dissolved, which results in general corrosion.
The results showed that the chemical stability of the carburized layer increases with increasing sintering temperature.
